<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via ExplainRequestSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/explain.mdx`  _(via ExplainRequestSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), explainAccessForCaller (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `31792d936466cf42e17100dec6b662fa7e49d8ff` — the merge of head `a805785ebc5b01f28caa0b61232151928acf5f0a` into base `84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 31792d936466cf42e17100dec6b662fa7e49d8ff && git checkout 31792d936466cf42e17100dec6b662fa7e49d8ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998 a805785ebc5b01f28caa0b61232151928acf5f0a && git checkout -B drift-repro 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998 && git merge --no-ff a805785ebc5b01f28caa0b61232151928acf5f0a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the record below, rendered on this head by an isolated reviewer at the contract-review tier. The seat orders S1–S4 (text and declaration) before landing; S5 is a follow-up.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c539133c622984659b7aeb34402c4f17f446f07`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, content/docs/references/security/explain.mdx, content/docs/references/api/record-page.mdx, .changeset/explain-self-refused-read-one-answer.md, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-self-refused-read-one-answer.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-asker-gate.test.ts, packages/rest/src/security-explain-self-refused-read-door.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Ruling of record.** Comment 6787890900 on #32004, first bullet: a caller whose read of an object is refused gets the same explanation for every record id, naming the read refusal and the layer that refused, and it replaces ruling C of #22851 for that caller. The diff implements that bullet for the explain surface and nothing else from the ruling.
- **Every door reaches the rule.** Every caller of the engine was read: REST `POST` and `GET /security/explain` (singular, batch, and the per-id fallback), the record-page explain part, and the in-process consumers all go through the one service entry. A request either names another user (the third-party arm, where a refused read was already "cannot read") or is a self-explanation and is handed the classified read. There is no third arm.
- **Principal kinds and context shapes.** Recognition reads the request alone, so it holds for a human, an agent, a context with no kind, and a caller naming its own id explicitly. An unidentified caller is refused at the REST door before the engine. An empty or foreign `userId` goes to the third-party arm. I found no context shape that escapes recognition.
- **Stored id against missing id.** Under a refused self-read the engine withholds the stored row from the record pass, so every per-layer attribution is the missing record's. The decider comes from a read-operation pass that is refused the same way. The preface reads no record. Singular and batch agree; the batch returns verdicts only.
- **Third-party asker and reader.** The third-party branch is the one `main` takes, and a reader's classified read maps to the same two outcomes as before. Flag (3) holds by reading.
- **Fault path.** A store fault in the self-read rejects and fails the explanation, singular and batch. Any declared refusal status lands on the not-visible answer. I found no fail-open path.
- **Check-runs at read time.** Check Changeset, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, the PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Spec property liveness are green. Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates) and the UI suites were still in progress. Flag (5) hands the full rest and spec suites to CI, so they are not yet evidenced on this head.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: none` is on both the PR body and the changeset, and `none` is right: no authorable key, value or type moves. Under the repo rule a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker; the changeset has `patch` on both packages, the banner, the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker and a "What to do" line. Level correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag (1)** (self recognised from the request): enforced as stated. Not blocking.
- **Flag (2)** (no named layer leaves `decidedBy` out; a fault still fails): enforced as stated and pinned at engine level. The published reference text overstates it; see ④ S4. Not blocking.
- **Flag (3)** (third party and reader unchanged): holds for the explain answer. One knock-on outside explain is undeclared; see ④ S1.
- **Flag (4)** (published `explainAccess` keeps absent-only behaviour): confirmed that no door calls it. Follow-up, not blocking; the consumer-facing text does not say it; see ④ S2.
- **Flag (5)** (local verification narrowed): accepted as declared. Landing waits on the in-progress checks named in ①; this record does not vouch for them.
- **Flag (6)** (a separate existence question at another door): not graded, as instructed. Nothing in this PR's claim depends on it.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts` against the ruling and its first consumer.** The contract text for `recordIds`, `record` and `decidedBy` states the ruled rule, and the service enforces it. The two generated references carry the same strings as the schema. No must-fix.

- **S1, should-fix: an undeclared knock-on narrowing at two other doors.** The attachment gate and the comment gate admit a parent edit on this surface's record verdict for `update`. A self caller whose context is not a person's, who holds a write grant but whose read is refused, moves from a record story to the not-visible answer, so those gates now refuse it. People already got that answer on `main`. The direction is fail-closed and matches those doors' stated rule, but the PR body says the data doors do not move and the changeset is silent. Declare it in the changeset and pin it. Read from the code, not measured.
- **S2, should-fix: the carve-out for the published engine export is missing from the shipped text.** `explainAccess(deps, input)` returns the same decision type the spec text now describes without exception, yet keeps the earlier answer for a refused read. The PR body says so; the changeset and the spec text do not. State the carve-out in both, or open the follow-up that gives the export the rule.
- **S3, should-fix: two docblocks in the same package still state the replaced rule.** The contract docblock on `SecurityPlugin#explainAccessForCaller`, which the changed body file names as its contract, and the docblock on `unreadableUnderCallerRead` both still say a self-explainer keeps the write path's notion. Both ship in the package's declarations and are false at this head. They are outside the diff, so read and not reviewed, but this PR is what falsifies them.
- **S4, should-fix: the generated reference states the decider without its exception.** The `describe` strings for `record` and `decidedBy` say the decider is the layer that refused the read. The code and the jsdoc leave it out when no read layer names the refusal. Carry the "omitted when no layer names it" clause into both strings and regenerate.
- **S5, should-fix (follow-up): the one-answer property rests on an unpinned assumption.** The code assumes a read refusal is a fact of the object and never of a record. I found no platform path that breaks it, and the two pinned shapes are object-level. If it were broken, [detail held by the security seat], the two ids would be answered differently, and for a person that would be a step back from `main`. Pin the assumption or classify at object level. Not demonstrated.
- **N1, nit:** the other-user condition in `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` repeats a conjunct the new constant already carries.
- **N2, nit:** no pin for a caller naming its own id explicitly, or for a delegated agent context; both take the pinned path by reading.
- **N3, nit:** the `record` description dropped the clause that a self-explainer cannot read an id its read finds no row for; the jsdoc keeps it.

**Implementing files against the contract.** `explain-engine.ts` and `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` agree with the spec text apart from S4. The tests pin two refused-read shapes, three context kinds, eight operations, the batch, both REST verbs, a reader control, a third-party control and the fault path. The ablation in the PR body is credible but not re-run here.

No must-fix. The five should-fix items are text, declaration and follow-up; none makes a stored id and a missing id answer differently on any door I could reach by reading.

**VERDICT: PASS**

The seat adopts the delta record below, rendered on this head by the same isolated reviewer at the contract-review tier. F1 is filed before landing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a805785ebc5b01f28caa0b61232151928acf5f0a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts + .changeset/explain-self-refused-read-one-answer.md, content/docs/references/security/explain.mdx, content/docs/references/api/record-page.mdx, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-self-refused-read-one-answer.test.ts

Delta record: this judges `9c539133c6..a805785ebc` against the findings of my record on `9c539133c6` (comment 6800400746). The engine and the explain-access arm are unchanged in the delta, so the judgments of that record on them stand.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What the delta is.** Two commits: text, declarations, one added pin block, and the regenerated references. The only change in a non-test source file is two docblocks in `security-plugin.ts`; no executable line moved.
- **Generated references.** The two regenerated references carry the new schema strings word for word.
- **PR body.** Replaced; it is on this head and its Clause-② line matches the changeset's.
- **Check-runs on this head.** Every non-skipped check is green: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, TypeScript Type Check (workspace, source, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint & Repo Gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness and the UI suites. One re-run of Check Changeset, started when the body was replaced, was still in progress beside a completed green run. The earlier flag (5) gap, the full rest and spec suites, is now evidenced by CI.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on both packages, BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker. The Clause-② line now also names the two gates that follow the verdict. Those gates' packages are not bumped, which is right: their code does not change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **S1: accepted deviation, closed as declared.** The changeset and PR body now state that the comment and attachment gates follow the `update` verdict and refuse a caller who holds edit while its read is refused. The wording is scoped to where those gates judge by the caller's own explanation, which matches the code. The "What to do" line tells the operator the remedy.
- **S1, placement of the pin: acceptable.** The pin sits on the explanation the gates read, for all three context kinds, with a reader control. It discriminates this head from `main` for the two non-person kinds. The gates' code is unchanged, so what moved is their input, and that is what is pinned. The remaining gap is that the admit condition is restated in the test, not imported from either gate; a later change to a gate's own condition would not trip it. That is a change to those gates and theirs to pin. Follow-up, not blocking.
- **S2: closed.** The carve-out for the engine export is in the changeset, in the spec JSDoc for `recordIds` and `record`, and in the `record` description.
- **S3: closed.** Both docblocks state the ruled rule and agree with the code.
- **S4: closed.** Both `describe` strings carry the omitted-decider clause, and the references follow.
- **S5: open as a declared follow-up.** It is listed in the PR body's acceptance notes, at rule level. It is not yet a tracked issue; see ④ F1.
- **N1: accepted with the stated reason.** The repeated conjunct is what narrows the id's type inside that arm; the named constant alone does not. The reason holds by reading.
- **N2: open, nit.** Still no pin for a caller naming its own id, or for a delegated agent context. Unchanged; not blocking.
- **N3: closed.** The no-row clause for a self-explainer is back in the `record` description.
- **The separate existence question at another door:** not graded.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts` against the ruling and the code.** Every sentence added in the delta is enforced at this head: the decider is omitted for every id when no read layer names the refusal (pinned at engine level), the self no-row case is "cannot read", and the engine export keeps its earlier answer. The new public text in the changeset, the spec, the references and the PR body stays at rule level; none of it names how a stored id could be told from a missing one.

- **F1, should-fix (follow-up): S5 has no tracked home.** The follow-up exists only as a line in the PR body, which stops being read once the PR lands. File it as an issue before or at landing. The underlying assumption is unchanged: [detail held by the security seat]. Not demonstrated on any platform path.
- **F2, nit: the spec description names another package's export.** The `record` description now ends with a sentence about the plugin-security engine export. It is accurate, but it also lands in the record-page reference, where that export has no reader. The JSDoc and the changeset already carry the carve-out; the sentence could leave the description. No effect on correctness or the contract.
- **F3, nit: the parent-edit pin restates the gates' admit condition.** See S1 above; a shared helper or a per-gate pin would close it when either gate gets a rig with the real security service.

**Implementing files in the delta.** The docblocks agree with the engine. The added pin block asserts the object-level answer is allowed while the record verdict is not visible, decided by the read's refusal, for a stored and a missing id alike.

No must-fix. S1 to S4 and N3 are resolved; N1 is accepted; S5, N2 and the three items above are follow-ups or nits.
